quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Before Maria goes to the market, she writes a shopping list. She checks the kitchen to see what is already there. At the store, she buys only what is on the list, so she spends less and forgets nothing.
options: A Guide to Choosing Fresh Fruit
quests.hint: Ask what Maria does before she leaves home, and what that step helps her do later.
quests.explanation: Each sentence belongs to one plan: write a list, check the kitchen, then buy only what is needed. A good title names the plan that connects the sentences.
quests.whyThisTitle: It names the list that links checking the kitchen with buying only what is needed.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Ken takes the number 12 bus to work. It leaves at 7:40, so he reaches the stop ten minutes early. On the ride he reads a book. When he gets to the office, he feels calm and ready.
options: Ken's First Day at a New Job
Ken Buys a Monthly Train Pass
quests.hint: Look for the one activity that Ken repeats, and notice what he does during it.
quests.explanation: The departure time, the waiting, and the reading all happen around one bus trip. The title that covers all of them is stronger than one about a job or a different way of traveling.
quests.whyThisTitle: The time, the stop, and the book all belong to the bus ride, so this title covers everything in the passage.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: To borrow books from the town library, you need a library card. Bring an ID and fill in a short form at the front desk. The card is free, and it works for books, movies, and music.
options: A Guide to Choosing a Book to Borrow
quests.hint: The passage tells you what to bring and what to do. What is the goal of those steps?
quests.explanation: The passage lists what you need and where to go so that you can get one item. That item, the card, is the center of the passage.
quests.whyThisTitle: Bringing an ID, filling in a form, and knowing the card is free all explain how to get the card.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Saturday is laundry day at Priya's house. She puts white shirts in one pile and dark jeans in another. Colorful towels make a third pile. Sorting first keeps the whites clean and stops colors from running together.
quests.hint: Focus on the step Priya takes before any water is used.
quests.explanation: All three piles are examples of one step that happens before washing. The other titles describe steps the passage never reaches.
quests.whyThisTitle: The piles of whites, darks, and towels are all part of sorting, and the passage stops at that step.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Every Saturday morning, the town square fills with small tents. Farmers sell tomatoes, eggs, and fresh bread. Musicians play near the fountain, and neighbors stop to talk. People come to shop, but many also come to meet friends.
options: Life at a Lively Weekend Market
A Quiet Evening at the Library
A Busy Day at the Airport
quests.correctAnswer: Life at a Lively Weekend Market
quests.hint: Think about what all the different scenes in the square have in common.
quests.explanation: Food stalls, music, and conversation all describe the same busy place. The correct title covers the whole scene, not just one thing that is sold.
quests.whyThisTitle: Stalls, music, and neighbors chatting all add up to one lively market, which the title names.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: To make a good cup of tea, start with fresh water. Heat it until it bubbles, then pour it over the tea bag. Wait three minutes before taking the bag out. Add milk or honey if you like.
options: A Guide to Choosing the Best Coffee Beans
quests.hint: The sentences follow one another in order. What is being made from start to finish?
quests.explanation: The passage moves in steps from water to the finished drink. A title should name the result of those steps, not a tool used along the way.
quests.whyThisTitle: Heating water, steeping, and adding milk all lead to one finished drink, so the title names that whole task.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Dr. Lee's dental office called to remind Sam about his visit on Tuesday at 3:00. Sam should arrive ten minutes early to fill in a short form. He also needs to bring his insurance card and a list of any medicines he takes.
options: Brushing Your Teeth Twice a Day
Getting Ready for a Dental Visit
quests.correctAnswer: Getting Ready for a Dental Visit
quests.hint: Ask what event all of these reminders are preparing Sam for.
quests.explanation: The time, the form, the card, and the medicine list are all preparation for one appointment. The title should name the appointment and the preparation.
quests.whyThisTitle: Every reminder in the passage is about getting ready for Sam's appointment at the dental office.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Houseplants need care, but not too much. Most like a bright window and water about once a week. Touch the soil first: if it feels wet, wait a few days. Too much water can hurt a plant more than too little.
options: A Guide to Choosing Flowers for a Gift
quests.hint: Look at what the last three sentences all tell you to do with water.
quests.explanation: The window and the soil test both connect back to water. The title should name the care task the whole passage explains.
quests.whyThisTitle: The soil test, the weekly schedule, and the warning about too much water all describe how to water well.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A new family moved in next door last week. Mr. Ortiz brought them a plate of cookies and said hello. He told them where the nearest grocery store is and which day the trash is collected. The family felt welcome right away.
quests.hint: Think about why Mr. Ortiz did each of these things.
quests.explanation: The cookies and the helpful information are both ways of making someone feel welcome. The trash day is only one small piece of that.
quests.whyThisTitle: The cookies, the greeting, and the local tips all show one act of welcoming, which the title names.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The weather report says heavy rain is coming this afternoon. Lena puts an umbrella in her bag and wears waterproof shoes. She also packs a plastic bag for her wet coat. When the rain starts, she is ready.
options: How to Choose a Warm Winter Coat
quests.hint: What do the umbrella, the shoes, and the plastic bag all have in common?
quests.explanation: The three items are different, but they serve one goal: staying prepared for a rainy afternoon. A title should name that goal.
quests.whyThisTitle: Each item Lena packs prepares her for the coming rain, so the title names that shared purpose.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Soccer practice starts at 4:30 on Wednesdays. The players warm up by jogging around the field, then they practice passing in pairs. The coach ends each session with a short game. Everyone goes home tired but happy.
quests.hint: Follow the practice from beginning to end. What is the whole event?
quests.explanation: Warm-up, passing, and the final game are parts of one practice session. A title about shoes or a television match ignores what actually happens.
quests.whyThisTitle: The jog, the passing drills, and the short game make up one practice, so the title covers all of them.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A good school lunch gives students energy for the afternoon. Many parents pack a sandwich, a piece of fruit, and a small bottle of water. Nuts and cheese make healthy snacks, too. Colorful food also makes lunchtime more fun.
options: Growing Fruit in a School Garden
quests.hint: Ask who is packing the food and where it will be eaten.
quests.explanation: The foods listed are examples of one larger idea: what makes a lunch good for school. The title should name that idea rather than one food.
quests.whyThisTitle: Sandwiches, fruit, and snacks are all examples of what belongs in a healthy lunch for school.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Adam's phone battery often dies before dinner. Now he plugs it in every night before bed. He keeps a second charger in his backpack for long days away from home. His phone rarely runs out of power anymore.
quests.hint: Notice the problem at the beginning and how the rest of the passage answers it.
quests.explanation: The passage starts with a dying battery and then lists two ways Adam avoids it. The title should cover the problem and the solution together.
quests.whyThisTitle: Charging at night and carrying a second charger both address the problem of a phone running out of power.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Yuki needs to mail a birthday gift to her sister. At the post office, a worker weighs the box and tells her the price. Yuki writes the address clearly on the label and pays. The package will arrive in three days.
options: A Guide to Choosing a Birthday Gift
Writing a Letter to a Friend
quests.hint: Look at what actually happens at the post office, step by step.
quests.explanation: The gift is why Yuki goes, but the passage is about what she does there. Weighing, addressing, and paying are all part of sending a parcel.
quests.whyThisTitle: Weighing the box, writing the address, and paying are the steps of mailing, not of choosing a gift.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: On Sundays, Riverside Park is full of people. Children play on the swings, and some families have picnics on the grass. Others jog on the path along the river. The park is free, and everyone is welcome.
options: A Day at the Swimming Pool
quests.hint: Think about the place where all these activities happen.
quests.explanation: Swings, picnics, and jogging are separate activities, but they all happen in one place on one day. The best title names the place and the day.
quests.whyThisTitle: The swings, picnics, and jogging path are all pieces of a Sunday in the park.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: A tourist stopped Omar on the street and asked how to reach the museum. Omar told her to walk two blocks, turn left at the bakery, and look for a tall red building. She thanked him and went on her way.
options: Visiting a Museum for the First Time
quests.hint: The museum and the bakery are places in the story. Who is doing what for whom?
quests.explanation: The museum and the bakery are only landmarks. The passage is about Omar helping a stranger find her way.
quests.whyThisTitle: The blocks, the turn, and the red building are all parts of the directions Omar gives.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Three classmates meet in the library every Thursday to study for their science test. They read the notes aloud and ask each other questions. When one student does not understand something, the others explain it.
options: A Guide to Choosing a Science Project
quests.hint: Find the activity the three friends share, and why they do it together.
quests.explanation: Reading notes aloud and asking questions are ways of studying as a group. The library is only where they meet.
quests.whyThisTitle: Reading aloud, asking questions, and explaining to each other all describe studying together.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Nina's bicycle tire went flat on the way to work. She walked to a shop, where a mechanic found a small nail in the tire. He fixed the hole in fifteen minutes and checked the brakes as well. Nina rode home safely.
quests.hint: Start with the problem. What happened, and what solved it?
quests.explanation: The nail, the shop, and the repair all follow from one flat tire. The other titles talk about riding in general, which is not what happens here.
quests.whyThisTitle: The flat tire, the nail, and the quick repair all belong to the story of one fix.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Carlos is planning a surprise party for his friend. He invites people by message, orders a cake, and asks everyone to arrive before six o'clock. On the day, he hides the decorations until the last moment.
quests.hint: Ask why Carlos hides the decorations and asks guests to come early.
quests.explanation: Invitations, a cake, and hidden decorations are pieces of one project. Only the party itself covers all of them.
quests.whyThisTitle: The messages, the cake, and the hiding all serve one plan, a party the friend does not expect.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: At the airport, the first step is to check in for your flight. Show your passport at the desk, leave your large bag, and get your boarding pass. Then go through security and find your gate. Arriving two hours early gives you time for each step.
options: How to Choose a Seat on the Plane
What to Do at the Airport
Packing a Suitcase for a Trip
quests.correctAnswer: What to Do at the Airport
quests.hint: Follow the order of actions. Where does everything take place?
quests.explanation: Check-in, security, and finding the gate all happen at the airport before a flight. Packing and seat choice happen elsewhere or are never mentioned.
quests.whyThisTitle: The passage walks through each stop inside the airport, so this title covers all the steps.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Ben started knitting last winter. His first scarf had holes and uneven edges, but he kept going. Now he makes hats for his family and can finish a small one in a weekend. He says knitting helps him relax.
quests.hint: Compare how Ben's work looked at the start with how it looks now.
quests.explanation: The passage follows Ben from a rough first scarf to hats he makes easily. That change over time is the core of the passage.
quests.whyThisTitle: The title follows Ben's progress from his first messy scarf to skilled knitting.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Mia needs to send a report to her manager by noon. She reads it once more, fixes two spelling mistakes, and saves the file. Then she attaches it to an email and clicks send. A minute later, her manager replies with a thank-you.
options: Sending a Report to a Manager
Writing a Long Email to a Friend
quests.correctAnswer: Sending a Report to a Manager
quests.hint: Notice who receives the work and what Mia does before sending it.
quests.explanation: Checking, saving, attaching, and sending are all steps in getting one report to one person. The title should name that task.
quests.whyThisTitle: Every action, from fixing mistakes to clicking send, is part of delivering the report.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The town will close Maple Street for repairs next Monday and Tuesday. Cars will have to use Oak Road instead. Buses will still run, but they will stop one block away. The work should finish by Wednesday morning.
options: A New Bus Route Through Town
quests.hint: Ask what event is announced and which street it affects.
quests.explanation: The detours and the bus change are effects of one event: repair work on Maple Street. The other titles pick out only a side detail or something not mentioned.
quests.whyThisTitle: The closure, detour, and bus change all follow from the repairs on Maple Street.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: The Kims used to trip over shoes at the front door. Now they keep a small shelf next to it, and each person has one space for their everyday shoes. The entrance looks tidy, and no one has to search for a missing pair.
options: A Shoe Shelf by the Front Door
quests.correctAnswer: A Shoe Shelf by the Front Door
quests.hint: Look at the problem the family had and the one thing they added.
quests.explanation: The family solves a messy entrance with one shelf. The title should name the change that fixes the problem.
quests.whyThisTitle: The shelf is the single change that explains both the tidy entrance and the end of missing shoes.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: On the first day of class, Teacher Sara asks every student to say their name and one thing they like. Some students are shy, but they smile and speak. By the end of the hour, everyone knows a few new faces.
options: A Guide to Choosing Classes for the Year
Meeting Classmates on the First Day
quests.correctAnswer: Meeting Classmates on the First Day
quests.hint: Ask what the class is doing instead of studying a subject.
quests.explanation: The activity is about introductions, not lessons. The title should name that activity and when it happens.
quests.whyThisTitle: Saying names and interests on day one is how the students meet each other.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: At the café, Jo looks at the menu for a minute and orders soup with a small salad. The server writes it down and repeats the order. Ten minutes later, the food arrives hot. Jo pays at the counter and leaves a small tip.
quests.hint: Follow Jo from the menu to the payment.
quests.explanation: Choosing, ordering, waiting, and paying make up one visit to a café. A title about cooking or working there would describe someone else's job.
quests.whyThisTitle: The passage covers every step of Jo's lunch order, from the menu to the tip.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Last Sunday, forty neighbors met at the corner of Pine Street with gloves and trash bags. They picked up bottles, paper, and old cans along the road. By noon, the street was clean, and the group shared sandwiches under a tree.
quests.hint: Think about who took part, what they did, and what changed by noon.
quests.explanation: The sandwiches are a pleasant ending, but most of the passage is about picking up trash together. The best title covers the group effort.
quests.whyThisTitle: The gloves, the bags, and the clean street all belong to one community cleanup.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Taking good photos is easier when you pay attention to light. Early morning and late afternoon give soft, warm light. Stand so the sun is beside you, not behind the subject. Try a few angles before you press the button.
options: How to Choose a New Camera
quests.hint: Each sentence gives advice. What skill is the advice for?
quests.explanation: The advice about light, position, and angles all helps you take better pictures. Buying, sharing, and printing are never discussed.
quests.whyThisTitle: The advice about time of day, sun position, and angles all points toward better photographs.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Leila bought a jacket that was too small. She took it back to the store the next day with her receipt. The clerk checked the tag and helped her exchange it for a larger size.
options: Returning a Jacket to the Store
How to Choose the Right Jacket Size
quests.correctAnswer: Returning a Jacket to the Store
quests.hint: Look at what Leila does after she discovers the problem.
quests.explanation: The size is the reason for the trip, but the passage is about taking the item back and swapping it. Choosing a size is only the last detail.
quests.whyThisTitle: The receipt, the clerk, and the swap describe the return, not the first purchase.

quests.instruction: Drag the best title for the passage.
quests.passage: Four coworkers who live in the same neighborhood now share one car to the office. They take turns driving each week. The trip is cheaper for everyone, and they find parking more easily. They also enjoy talking during the ride.
quests.hint: Ask what the four people do together, and why it helps each of them.
quests.explanation: Lower cost, easier parking, and conversation are all results of one arrangement. The title should name the arrangement, not just one benefit.
quests.whyThisTitle: Taking turns driving explains why the trip is cheaper, easier to park, and more social.
